input: st. louis sits right where the missouri river meets the mississippi. it was founded in 1764 by pierre laclede and auguste chouteau as a fur trading post. the gateway arch was finished on oct. 28, 1965 and opened to visitors in 1967. it's approx. 630 ft. tall and exactly as wide as it is tall, which is kind of neat. the city hosted the 1904 world's fair and the u.s. olympics that same year. those were the first olympics held in north america. the cardinals have won 11 world series titles, second only to the yankees. anheuser-busch has been brewing there since 1852. the city is famous for chuck berry was from there and played monthly shows at blueberry hill for years. the city separated from st. louis county in 1876, which still confuses people. the population peaked around 857,000 in 1950 and has dropped a lot since then. summers are humid and winters can get pretty cold. the metrolink light rail connects the airport to downtown and the illinois side. the old courthouse is where the dred scott case was first heard in 1847. the eads bridge opened in 1874 and was the first major steel truss bridge in the world. the city's nickname is the gateway to the west, which is where the arch gets its name. t.s. eliot, maya angelou, and josephine baker all grew up there at some point. the blues won their first stanley cup in 2019 after being the worst team in the league in jan. union station was once the largest and busiest passenger rail terminal in the world. it's now a hotel with an aquarium and a ferris wheel next to it. the city has a big bosnian community, one of the largest
